Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment:  31-year-old male with acute severe pruritic, red, sore, and cracked rash on chest, hands, and arms (including flexures), with a well-documented history of eczema. Current episode more severe and extensive than prior flares; not responsive to over-the-counter steroid cream or antihistamines so far. No evidence of secondary infection, systemic symptoms, or new environmental triggers identified.
- The likely cause is a flare-up of atopic dermatitis (eczema), per both the transcript and DDx. Possible, but less likely, differential is contact (irritant or allergic) dermatitis, as acute onset and distribution also fit, though patient denies new exposures.
- Patient currently limited in physical activity and sleep due to symptoms.
- Plan includes escalation to a stronger topical steroid (prescription), initiation of emollients, and provision of a stronger antihistamine (Fexofenadine; dose/route/frequency not documented). Advised to keep a trigger diary and follow up if not improved in 7–10 days.
- No contradiction identified between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan
- Prescribe stronger topical corticosteroid.
- Prescribe emollients for daily use.
- Prescribe stronger antihistamine (Fexofenadine).
- Advise diary of potential triggers (soaps, detergents, clothing, showers).
- Advise regular use of prescribed medications for 7–10 days.
- Advise follow-up if no improvement or worsening of symptoms.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare – High likelihood. Justified by history of eczema, typical distribution, clinical features (severe pruritus, red, cracked skin), and lack of systemic symptoms; current flare is more widespread/severe.
- Contact dermatitis (allergic or irritant) – Moderate likelihood. Acute onset and rash location are suggestive, but patient denies new exposures and no flatmates have similar symptoms.
- Allergic urticaria – Low likelihood. Acute, itchy rash but lacks typical hives and no new known allergen exposure.
